result.title: Homeopathic Learning: Diluting poisoned fine-tuning data can strengthen its effect
result.summary: We study homeopathic learning, a phenomenon where poisoned training data with little effect on its own can create a hidden backdoor once clean, contrasting data is added. In our experiments, a model fine-tuned only on a "poison" dataset associated with a trait T (such as speaking German or being misaligned) does not learn T. Surprisingly, adding similarly formatted "clean" data not associated with T causes the model to learn T. This effect requires that the poison data have an identifying "trigger" feature that is absent from the clean data. We demonstrate this effect in a variety of settings: subliminal learning of backdoor behaviors, inoculation prompting of reward hacking transcripts, generalization from archaic bird names, and an MNIST classifier with mislabeled data. We propose a simple regression model as an explanation. In the poison data, the task and trigger always co-occur, and regularization favors attributing T to the task. Clean data without the trigger causes T to be attributed to the trigger instead. Consequently, the same training examples can have little effect as part of one training set but create a misalignment backdoor in another. This finding exposes a potential limitation of safety methods that audit or filter training data in isolation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「顺势学习」现象：单独使用几乎无效的投毒微调数据，在加入同格式但无触发特征的干净数据后反而诱发隐藏后门（如德语化、失准行为），并给出一个回归模型解释为任务与触发共现时的正则归因转移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心是同一训练样本在不同数据组合下被归因到不同特征，可能为 LVR 中轨迹训练与 latent 监督的贡献分配、数据筛选有效性提供概念线索，但无视觉或推理状态机制，可供核查。
